Overall, it was a wonderful experience, and I highly recommend visiting the temple for anyone seeking peace, devotion, and spiritual upliftment.

customer_updates.name: Deepak Salian
customer_updates.text:
Mini Sabarimala, situated on a hillock surrounded by hills and valleys within the precincts of NCH Colony, Kanjurmarg (West), Mumbai, is the first ancient Ayyappa Temple outside Kerala State.As revealed by the astrologer Shri Karuvatta Kochugovindan, there was a big Devi temple and a small Ayyappa temple at this place, where today stands the temple of Shree Mini Sabarimala. These temples were destroyed by the foreign invaders. The remnants of these can be seen even today. The invaders also killed the priests of these temples.

Since then the devotees used to worship Shri Ayyappa in the same dilapidated temple.

featured_reviews.name: Harish Nair
featured_reviews.review_text: This Holy Abode of Lord Ayyappa is one of the oldest outside Kerala, it is located on hill hock situated inside Naval Civilian Housing Colony. Entry is restricted and is bound by NCHS rules. Temple timings are in general similar to ones in Kerala, morning 04.30 am to 10.00 am evening 04.30 am to 8.00 pm (timings to checked as it might changes, on special occasions this might change). The locations is by far the best one can find around any temple in Mumbai, area is covered with thick vegetation, vehicle can reach up to foot hill, a small trek of 100-150 steps would be required to reach the temple. It has sanctums of God Shiva, Rama, Hanuman, Ganapati & Devi. Main deity is God Ayyappa.- Temples host various cultural events, bhajan, poojas, recitals, congregation saptahams & Annual temple festive. Varied Poojas for individuals and families cane be performed here. The ambience is very appealing, even though situated inside the city it provides a escape from city hustle, silence and environment is ideal for calmly the sensory, can indulge in bhakti & deep mediation without any hinderance. Can be reached via train (Railway Station Kanjurmarg with in 1 km), BUSES, Auto, Private vehicles.

Suvarna Temple is also known as "Shree Mahashesha Rundamalini Temple" or "Nine Mother Children Temple" and is indeed a unique temple in its own. Located amidst the beauty of Powai this temple has lot of serenity and calm. The ‘Nine Mother Children’ temple is one of the oldest holy places in Powai. This temple was evolved in 1957, but the prathista and other ritual ceremony were performed on 1963. Here you can find all the almighties from all the communities-Hindus, Muslim, Chirstian. So the restriction is not imparted on any caste to enter inside the premises. Here all the caste and religion are treated one and the same.

featured_reviews.name: arti mogadpally
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visiting the Suvarna Naga Temple in Powai was a deeply peaceful and spiritually uplifting experience. Tucked away amidst greenery and the calm surroundings of Powai, the temple offers a soothing escape from the noise and rush of city life. As soon as I entered the temple premises, I felt a sense of serenity and positive energy.
The temple is dedicated to Lord Suvarna Naga, and the idol is beautifully adorned, reflecting devotion and purity. The architecture is simple yet graceful, allowing devotees to focus entirely on prayer and meditation. The priests perform the rituals with great dedication, and they patiently guide devotees through the puja process, explaining its significance.
What touched me the most was the calm atmosphere inside the temple. The sound of bells, chants, and incense created a spiritually charged environment that helped me feel connected and grounded. Many devotees visit the temple seeking relief from Naga dosha and for overall well-being, and the faith here feels strong and genuine.
Overall, my visit to Suvarna Naga Temple, Powai, was a fulfilling experience. It left me with inner peace, positivity, and a sense of gratitude. I would highly recommend this temple to anyone looking for spiritual solace and divine blessings in Mumbai.
